recent: the operating booth of a small vintage planetarium before a community costume evening, a compact hand-cranked pinhole star projector and curved dark ceiling dotted with a few unlabelled projected stars; warm practical lamps, no science laboratory or live-music stage — she patiently aligns a tiny star projector, an everyday echo of the dying stars from which her element came. an empty nostalgic bowling alley just before opening, polished wooden lanes in soft morning light and a low mechanical ball-return rail with one dense charcoal-black ball; no readable scores, signs or numerals — at an adult retro costume club event she tries to coax an unexpectedly heavy bowling ball out of the return cradle, amused that an ordinary pastime has become a small exercise in managing dense weight. As she lowers into a stable squat, the concertina pleats of her short outer apron fan apart over the fully opaque fitted shorts, showing more upper leg through movement, with no wind, wet fabric, undone fasteners or slipped shoulder strap

a quiet apartment's luggage-packing nook at early morning, an open hard-sided suitcase lined with thick folded towels on a low bench, plain shelves and soft window light; no laboratory, garden, palace or waterfront — she carefully settles a surprisingly heavy antique green-glass serving bowl into the padded suitcase, taking the same care with a household heirloom that she would with immense contained power. a small domestic sewing nook with a foot-powered sewing machine and a basket of mending — checking the hem of a repaired knee stocking while sitting; one knee raised naturally draws the scalloped side hem upward, showing more outer thigh with full intimate coverage

a quiet community music room with an upright glass harmonica in a sunlit bay window — testing the rim of one glass bowl with a damp fingertip and listening to its note, the other hand turning a small water tap
a hilltop observatory with its dome open to a clear night sky — standing
a busy street market of food stalls and strung bulbs — holds a palm-sized raw quartz crystal whose one end is cut and polished into a gleaming silicon chip in both hands in front of her
an old stone chapel lit by candles — brings a small bouquet up to her face to smell the flowers
her living room with a deep sofa — stitches into a small embroidery hoop with fabric in it
a kitchen or galley in her element's kingdom — seated on a chair
a Roman marble bath hall — lying on her front
a sunlit white marble temple — holds a small sealed glass vial of clear oil at chest height
a refinery yard of silver storage tanks — swirls the liquid in a round glass flask with a slow circling motion
